content.title: Create an object
Read a property
content.text:
```js
user.name
```

This produces `"Maya"`.

You can also use bracket notation:

```js
user["age"]
```

This produces `24`.

content.title: Update
content.text:
Objects can hold changing data:

```js
user.age = 25;
```

After this line, `user.age` is `25`.

content.prompt:
Create an object named `book` with:

- `title`: `"The Long Way"`
- `pages`: `320`

Then read the title property.

feedback.incorrect: Check the requirements and compare your code with the expected structure.

content.question: When is an object more useful than an array?

options.text: When the data is best understood through named properties.
When the values must always be in numerical order.
When there can only be one value.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. When the data is best understood through named properties.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. When the data is best understood through named properties.

takeaways: **Mental model:** Arrays answer "which position?" Objects answer "which named property?"
**Senior habit:** Choose a data shape that makes the intended meaning obvious to the next person reading the code.
nextSteps: Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
